terms.gloss: adze, the carpenter’s axe for dressing timber
evidence: Plin. NH 7.198: fabricam māteriāriam Daedalus et in eā serram, asciam, perpendiculum, terebram
Plin. NH 16.207: mollissima tilia … quod citissimē asciās retundat
Vitr. 7.2.2: sūmātur ascia et, quemadmodum māteria dolātur, sīc calx in lacū mācerāta asciētur
Libellus VII, Diēs ūnus Osoitsae, gloss: secūris fabrī quā trabēs dolantur
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “an axe for hewing wood, a carpenter’s axe”; secūris is the ordinary axe. Pliny, NH 7.198 makes Daedalus the inventor of carpentry and of its first tools; the square and the level go to Theodorus of Samos. In NH 16.207 lime wood blunts adzes fastest. In Vitruvius 7.2.2 the adze also tests slaked lime: if the lime clings to the iron like glue, it is ready for plastering.

phrases.english: I know the adze! I want the adze!

phrases.latin: malleus, serra, ascia, quam Bulgarī teslam vocant, secūris, terebra, scalprum, rēgula, norma, forceps, runcīna, trulla, quā tēctōrēs tēctōrium indūcunt, līnea cum perpendiculō, capsa clāvōrum
phrases.english: hammer, saw, the adze the Bulgarians call tesla, axe, drill, chisel, ruler, square, pincers, plane, the trowel plasterers spread plaster with, a plumb line, a box of nails
